cards.explanation: The answer is the saints. Paul says it plainly: “…how dare he go to law before the unrighteous instead of before the saints!” He wants the grievance kept among believers. Think of it as settling things at your own kitchen table before calling in a stranger to referee.

The answer is True. Paul asks it like it's obvious: “Do you not know that the saints will judge the world?” He's reminding the Corinthians how big their calling is. I'd say that's the kind of question that makes you sit up straight at the table, friends.

The word is trivial. Paul asks, “And if you are to judge the world, are you not competent to judge trivial cases?” His point is that if they can handle the big job, the small stuff should be no trouble. It's like being trusted with the whole kitchen and then panicking over a crooked cookie.

The answer is angels. Paul asks, “Do you not know that we will judge angels?” Then he adds, “How much more the things of this life!” If you'll be doing that, a squabble over everyday stuff is a pretty light load, friends.

The answer is someone wise enough to settle it between brothers. Paul asks, “Is there really no one among you wise enough to arbitrate between his brothers?” He says it to their shame. I think he's hoping somebody in that church stands up and says, “I'll help.”

The word is unbelievers. Paul says, “Instead, one brother goes to law against another, and this in front of unbelievers!” So the dispute is out in the open for people outside the church to watch. That's the part that gets him going.

The answer is True. Paul says, “The very fact that you have lawsuits among you means that you are thoroughly defeated already.” It's about having the lawsuits at all, before anyone even wins. Having a winner doesn't change that.

The answer is to let themselves be wronged, and that's the hard one. Paul asks, “Why not rather be wronged? Why not rather be cheated?” It's tough to hear. I think letting something go instead of taking it to court is one of the hardest things there is, and that's the question he asks.

The answer is that they're cheating and wronging their own brothers. Paul says, “Instead, you yourselves cheat and do wrong, even against your own brothers!” They were asked why they wouldn't take being wronged, and they were the ones doing it. I think that line hits close to home.
The answer is False. Paul asks, “Do you not know that the wicked will not inherit the kingdom of God?” Then he warns, “Do not be deceived…” He wants the Corinthians to see it clearly, friends.

The answer is True. After the list Paul says, “And that is what some of you were.” Notice the word were. It tells us where they started and sets up what comes next. That's good news waiting right around the corner.

The answer is that they were washed and made holy and right with God. Paul says, “But you were washed, you were sanctified, you were justified…” That's three big words, all pointing to what was done for them. It's one of my favorite turns in the whole letter.

The answer is the Spirit of our God. Paul says it was “…in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and by the Spirit of our God.” Both are named together there. When I think of the day someone reached into my drawer and called me out, I get a little misty myself, friends.
